statements.status_notes: vllm 0.28.0: remote/inline media fetched and decoded before size limits. Carriers: converter. Runtime use: Executed in-process: MinerU 4.0.7 builds vllm.LLM / AsyncLLM (mineru/model/vlm/runtime.py) and calls generate() with PIL page images rendered from the PDF by PDFium (docvortex) and fixed MinerU prompts and sampling parameters. No OpenAI-compatible server, no Rust frontend, no KV connector, no disaggregated serving, no trust_remote_code. The container runs with network_mode: none, started per job by convert-job.sh. Model: the pinned MinerU 2.5 Pro VLM from the verified payload. No Ghostscript in the image.
statements.impact_statement: No URL or base64 media; images are in-memory PIL objects and the container has no network. MinerU runs vLLM in-process (vllm.LLM / AsyncLLM); the OpenAI-compatible HTTP server and its request fields do not exist in the converter, which also has no network (network_mode: none).

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-68770
vulnerability.description: sentence-transformers local model loading bypasses trust_remote_code and executes custom Python

statements.status_notes: sentence-transformers 5.3.0: import_module_class trust gate bypassed when the model path exists locally (modules.json custom code runs with trust_remote_code=False). Carriers: builder; full/model_bridge (source only), kb-tools linux-line engine (build host). Runtime use: Imported (rag_core.orchestrator imports retrievers.colbert, which imports pylate, which imports sentence_transformers). Model load: pylate.models.ColBERT(model_name_or_path="lightonai/Agent-ModernColBERT", trust_remote_code=False) from the root-owned image config. The ColBERT model is not on the alpha.2 media and the builder is offline, so the retriever reports itself degraded.
statements.impact_statement: The bypass needs model_name_or_path to be an existing local directory an attacker can write. Deep32 passes the hub id "lightonai/Agent-ModernColBERT" from root-owned image config (cwd root-owned), the ColBERT model is not on the alpha.2 media, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 blocks fetching, and a config override is an owner action on the owner's data root.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2
vulnerability.description: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys

statements.status_notes: certifi 2026.7.22: bundled emSign ECC Root CA - G3 trusted (compromised eMudhra intermediates). Carriers: builder; Workstation deep32-engine and deep32-gateway venvs (disc 1); full gateway (source only), kb-tools linux-line (build host), tests/engine and tests/gateway dev pins. Runtime use: Imported by httpx/requests; httpx loads the bundle into an SSL context when a client is built. No TLS connection is verified against it: Forge containers speak plain HTTP on internal Docker networks with no outside route; on the Workstation the engine reaches the Forge through the GPU forwarder over UNIX sockets (http://), and the forwarder (serve_accel.py) uses stdlib ssl with GPU_EXT_CA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem (the OpenBSD bundle); the gateway sits behind Tailscale Serve and calls the engine locally over HTTP.
statements.impact_statement: No component verifies a TLS connection against the certifi bundle at runtime (see runtime note). The Workstation's TLS connection to the Forge is made by the GPU forwarder with stdlib ssl and the OpenBSD bundle; the pairing and Ask links pin the certificate of the other end.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-126360
vulnerability.description: OpenTelemetry Python API: Denial of service through quadratic-time traceparent parsing

statements.status_notes: opentelemetry-api 1.45.0: traceparent extraction quadratic regex (CPU DoS); MCP _meta named as a path. Carriers: Workstation deep32-gateway venv (disc 1); full gateway (source only), kb-tools linux-line gateway (build host), tests/gateway dev pins. Runtime use: Executed per MCP request: mcp 2.2.0 (wheel sha256 bde98258..., equal to the lock hash) calls opentelemetry.propagate.extract(params._meta) in mcp/shared/_otel.py. The gateway mounts the MCP app behind its Guard middleware (tailnet address allow-list, then bearer-token check), with a 256 KiB request-body cap.
statements.impact_statement: Same path as GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h: only authenticated, allow-listed gateway clients reach extract().

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-114603
vulnerability.description: OpenTelemetry Python: Unbounded tracestate parsing in opentelemetry-api

statements.status_notes: opentelemetry-api 1.45.0: TraceState.from_header quadratic regex on a long tracestate (CPU DoS). Carriers: Workstation deep32-gateway venv (disc 1); full gateway (source only), kb-tools linux-line gateway (build host), tests/gateway dev pins. Runtime use: Executed per MCP request: mcp 2.2.0 (wheel sha256 bde98258..., equal to the lock hash) calls opentelemetry.propagate.extract(params._meta) in mcp/shared/_otel.py. The gateway mounts the MCP app behind its Guard middleware (tailnet address allow-list, then bearer-token check), with a 256 KiB request-body cap.
statements.impact_statement: Reached only through MCP params._meta after the gateway Guard has accepted the tailnet address and the bearer token. Only the owner's enrolled agents hold tokens; a token holder could stall the gateway event loop for seconds per request, which is less than the read access the token already grants.
